celestialTargets.name: Jezero Crater Delta
celestialTargets.summary: Noachian paleolake delta preserving Mg-carbonates, Fe/Mg-smectites, olivine-rich mafic floor units, and stratified mudstones.

celestialTargets.name: Gale Crater (Aeolis Mons)
celestialTargets.summary: Equatorial impact basin hosting lacustrine mudstones, hydrated Mg/Ca-sulfates, and basaltic aeolian bedforms.

celestialTargets.name: Olympus Mons Basal Escarpment
celestialTargets.summary: High-relief volcanic basal scarp with steep talus slopes, fresh mafic basalt flows, high rock abundance, and minimal phyllosilicate alteration.

celestialTargets.missionArchetype: Permanent Moon Base Peak of Eternal Light & ISRU

celestialTargets.name: Mare Tranquillitatis Skylight
celestialTargets.missionArchetype: Lunar Lava Tube Skylight & Habitat Vault
celestialTargets.summary: Collapsed high-Ti mare basalt skylight (~100 m deep) leading to an inferred ~45 m wide lava tube conduit with ~290 K stable thermal interior.

celestialTargets.name: Marius Hills Pit

celestialTargets.name: Aristarchus Plateau

earthSites.name: Erg Chebbi (Visual Anti-Analog)
earthSites.antiAnalogNote: Visual false-friend: iron-oxide coated pure quartz dunes (SiO2 ~93 wt%) mislead color imagery while lacking Martian mafic mineralogy, steep basalt talus, and hydrated salts.
earthSites.earthCoBenefits: Demonstrates why true planetary analog selection must verify orbital spectroscopy over RGB desert color.
citations: DOI: 10.1016/j.icarus.2013.09.020 (Farr et al., 2013; Planetary analog mineralogical pitfalls of quartz ergs)
